domains.proposed_domain: Riemannian geometry and optimal transport regularity

evidence.quote:
Fix $(M,g)$ as above and $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda<\infty$ for which the following density class is nonempty. There are $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on $(M,g),\lambda,\Lambda$, such that the following holds for every pair of measurable densities satisfying $$\int_M\rho_i\,d\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}=1,\qquad
 \lambda\leq\rho_i\leq\Lambda\quad\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}\text{-almost everywhere},
 \qquad i=0,1.$$ The almost-everywhere unique optimal map from $\rho_0\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}$ to $\rho_1\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}$ for the cost $c$ has a homeomorphic representative $\widetilde T:M\to M$, and $$d(\widetilde T(x),\widetilde T(x'))\leq C d(x,x')^\alpha,
 \qquad
 d(\widetilde T^{-1}(y),\widetilde T^{-1}(y'))
       \leq C d(y,y')^\alpha$$ for all $x,x',y,y'\in M$.

exclusions.reason: The guarantee concerns the stated continuous manifold and positive-density setting; a discrete computational guarantee is absent.

hypotheses.statement: Fix $(M,g)$ as above and $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda<\infty$ for which the following density class is nonempty.
There is a geometric constant $C_g$ such that the cost is uniformly semiconcave in either variable, including at cut points.
Let $p\in G_x$, and let $S_p(r)$ be the Jacobi tensor along $\exp_x(rp)$ with $S_p(0)=0$, $D_rS_p(0)=\mathrm{Id}$, in parallel orthonormal frames.
Let $p_i\in G_x$, $m_i>0$, $\sum_i m_i=1$, and set $p=\sum_i m_ip_i$, $E=\mathop{\mathrm{span}}\{p_i-p\}$.
Let $f$ be Lipschitz and semiconvex.

For every potential $u$, every $x\in M$, and every $p\in\partial u(x)$, one has $p\in G_x$ and $$u(x')\geq u(x)+c(x,\exp_xp)-c(x',\exp_xp)
 \qquad(x'\in M).$$ For each $0<t<1$, $F_t:\Gamma_u\to M$ is a homeomorphism, $tp\in I(x)$, and its poles are the unique global minimizers of $Q_tu$.
Both $G_x$ and $I(x)$ are convex for every $x\in M$.

For a dual pair $(u,v)$, each set $$\mathcal S_x(r)=\left\{p\in G_x:
      u(x)+\frac{|p|^2}{2}+v(\exp_xp)\leq r\right\}$$ is compact and convex, including ordinary and conjugate cut endpoints.
Let $(u,v)$ be a dual pair and $0<t<1$.
Let $\gamma(s)=\exp_x(sv)$ be a geodesic and identify its tangent spaces by parallel transport.

With a constant depending only on $(M,g)$, if $v\in G_x$ and $1/2\le\theta\le1$, then $$\label{spec:radial-det}
  \sigma_x(\theta v)\ge c\sigma_x(v).$$ Suppose $y=\exp_xp$, $p\in G_x$, and $\bar p=-P_{x\to y}p$.
There is $c_{\rm p}>0$, depending only on $(M,g)$, with the following property.
Assume weak MTW.
Assume weak MTW and the convexity of $G_x$ established in Corollary 7.

If there are $\beta>0$, $C_0<\infty$, and $r_0>0$ such that $F(r)\leq C_0r^\beta$ for $0<r<r_0$, then all the optimal maps in the fixed density class have homeomorphic representatives with a common Hölder estimate in both directions.
Suppose that $F$ has no power upper bound near zero.

There is a fixed smooth function $B_c:\mathbb R\to(-1,1)$ with bounded derivatives such that $$B_c'<0\text{ on }\mathbb R,\qquad
 B_c(s)\geq1-\varepsilon_0\quad(s\leq1/2),\qquad
 B_c(s)<0\quad(s\geq3/4).$$ Given a cap $M_0\geq2$ and $K\geq1$, there are $0<\eta\leq1/128$ and a smooth bounded function $B_o\geq0$, with bounded derivatives, satisfying $$\begin{aligned}
 &B_o(s)\geq1\quad(s\leq1-\eta),\qquad
 B_o(1)=0,\qquad 1\leq B_o(0)\leq1+\varepsilon_0,       \label{sc:outer-values}\\
 &B_o(s)\geq B_o(0)+1
       \quad(1/16\leq s\leq1-\eta),            \label{sc:barrier}\\
 &B_o'(s)>0,\quad B_o''(s)\leq-K
       \quad\text{if }-2\eta\leq s\leq1-\eta
                      \text{ and }B_o(s)\leq M_0.

For all sufficiently small selected scales, uniformly for $b\in[b_-,b_+]$, there is $$\frac b{32D}\leq\tau_b\leq\frac{8b}D
 \label{sc:switch-time}$$ such that, at $x_b=\exp_{x_0}(\tau_b p_0)$, the function $g_b$ has active endpoints $y_-$ and $y_+$ with $$-2\eta\leq s_{y_-}<1/16,\qquad s_{y_+}\geq1-\eta.$$ The original endpoints $y_0,y_1$ and every active endpoint at this pole lie in one original section $S_{C b}(x_b;u,v)$, where $C$ depends only on the geometry and $H_o$.
For all sufficiently small selected scales and all $b\in[b_-,b_+]$, $$c_0b\leq E(b)\leq b, \label{sc:excess-bounds}$$ with the constant in [sc:numerical], independently of $K$.
Fix a sufficiently small selected scale.

At any maximum in Lemma 22, let $$p=\sum_{i=1}^N m_i p_i,\qquad m_i>0,\qquad\sum_i m_i=1,$$ be any finite representation by minimizing logs active for the displayed representation $g_b=w_{o,b}^c$ at its minimizing pole $x$.
At a maximum in Lemma 22, the center and all active endpoints belong to $S_{(H_o+2)b}(x;u,v)$.
Suppose $p=\sum_{i=1}^N m_ip_i$ in an $n$-dimensional Euclidean space, with $N\leq n+1$, $m_i>0$, and $\sum_i m_i=1$.

Let $u,v$ be the dual potentials for an admissible pair of densities, and let $$\mathcal C=\{(x,y):u(x)+c(x,y)+v(y)=0\}.$$ For a Borel set $A$ on either side, its contact image satisfies $$\label{jet:contact-volume-eq}
 \frac{\lambda}{\Lambda}\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(A)
 \le \mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(\mathcal C(A))
 \le \frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(A).$$ Projections are interpreted in the completed volume measures.
Let $v$ be one of the original dual potentials.
Suppose $z_0$ is a point where $F$ has a second-order expansion and $x(z)$ is differentiable.
Fix one set of scales, one original potential $v$, and the two templates.
Fix $b>0$ and an active outer pair $$g_b(x)+c(x,y)+\varphi_o(v(y))=0.$$ Choose any minimizing reverse log $r$ from $y$ to $x$.

At a pair as in Lemma 30, let $p=\log_xy$ be the corresponding forward log, $B=(d\exp_x)_p$, and let $H_o\ge0$ be a lower Taylor Hessian, with zero linear part, of $d\mapsto w_o(\exp_x(p+d))+\tfrac12|p+d|^2$.

If $f$ is semiconvex near $0$ and has the Alexandrov expansion $$f(h)=f(0)+p\cdot h+\tfrac12 A(h,h)+o(|h|^2),$$ then every nearby subgradient satisfies $$\zeta=p+Ah+o(|h|),\qquad \zeta\in\partial f(h),$$ uniformly over the choice of $\zeta$.
Fix the center template and the constants of Lemmas 21, 22, 23, and 25.
Suppose the matrices and vectors satisfy [jet:limiting-geometry]–[jet:limiting-outer].

outputs.exact_statement:
Fix $(M,g)$ as above and $0<\lambda\leq\Lambda<\infty$ for which the following density class is nonempty. There are $\alpha\in(0,1]$ and $C<\infty$, depending only on $(M,g),\lambda,\Lambda$, such that the following holds for every pair of measurable densities satisfying $$\int_M\rho_i\,d\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}=1,\qquad
 \lambda\leq\rho_i\leq\Lambda\quad\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}\text{-almost everywhere},
 \qquad i=0,1.$$ The almost-everywhere unique optimal map from $\rho_0\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}$ to $\rho_1\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}$ for the cost $c$ has a homeomorphic representative $\widetilde T:M\to M$, and $$d(\widetilde T(x),\widetilde T(x'))\leq C d(x,x')^\alpha,
 \qquad
 d(\widetilde T^{-1}(y),\widetilde T^{-1}(y'))
       \leq C d(y,y')^\alpha$$ for all $x,x',y,y'\in M$.

There is a geometric constant $C_g$ such that the cost is uniformly semiconcave in either variable, including at cut points. Every potential is $D_g$-Lipschitz and uniformly semiconvex. For a continuous representing datum $w$, define $$\mathcal V_u(x)=\{p\in G_x:
              u(x)+c(x,\exp_xp)+w(\exp_xp)=0\}.$$ Then $\mathcal V_u(x)$ is compact and $\partial u(x)=\operatorname{conv}\mathcal V_u(x)$. Every $p\in\partial u(x)$ has a positive representation using at most $n+1$ affinely independent active logs. The set $\mathcal V_u(x)$ includes every minimizing log to each endpoint active for the specified datum $w$.

Let $p\in G_x$, and let $S_p(r)$ be the Jacobi tensor along $\exp_x(rp)$ with $S_p(0)=0$, $D_rS_p(0)=\mathrm{Id}$, in parallel orthonormal frames. For $0<t<s<1$, $$\frac{d}{dr}H_r(p)=-S_p(r)^{-1}S_p(r)^{-T},
 \qquad H_t(p)-H_s(p)\geq\kappa_g(s-t)\mathrm{Id},$$ where $\kappa_g>0$ depends only on the manifold. On every smooth minimizing branch, $A_x(w)w=w$.

Let $p_i\in G_x$, $m_i>0$, $\sum_i m_i=1$, and set $p=\sum_i m_ip_i$, $E=\mathop{\mathrm{span}}\{p_i-p\}$. If $t\operatorname{conv}\{p_i\}\subset I(x)$ and $0<t<s<1$, then $$\left[\frac{A_x(tp)}t-\sum_i m_i\frac{A_x(sp_i)}s\right]
       \bigg|_{E^\perp}\geq\kappa_g(s-t)\mathrm{Id}.$$ The conclusion also holds at a limiting time $t$ if the radially contracted hulls lie in $I(x)$ and the displayed Hessians have nonconjugate branch limits. No minimizing assumption about $sp$ is needed in this limiting assertion.

Let $f$ be Lipschitz and semiconvex. For sufficiently small $t>0$, depending only on these two bounds and the manifold, $$F_t:\Gamma_f\to M,\qquad
 \Gamma_f=\{(x,p):p\in\partial f(x)\},\qquad
 F_t(x,p)=\exp_x(tp)$$ is a homeomorphism with locally Lipschitz inverse into the tangent bundle. The minimizing pole $x_t(z)$ of $Q_tf$ is unique, $Q_tf\in C^{1,1}$, and $\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}Q_tf(z)=-t^{-1}\log_zx_t(z)$. The graph $\Gamma_f$ is an $n$-dimensional Lipschitz manifold.

For every potential $u$, every $x\in M$, and every $p\in\partial u(x)$, one has $p\in G_x$ and $$u(x')\geq u(x)+c(x,\exp_xp)-c(x',\exp_xp)
 \qquad(x'\in M).$$ For each $0<t<1$, $F_t:\Gamma_u\to M$ is a homeomorphism, $tp\in I(x)$, and its poles are the unique global minimizers of $Q_tu$.
Both $G_x$ and $I(x)$ are convex for every $x\in M$.

For a dual pair $(u,v)$, each set $$\mathcal S_x(r)=\left\{p\in G_x:
      u(x)+\frac{|p|^2}{2}+v(\exp_xp)\leq r\right\}$$ is compact and convex, including ordinary and conjugate cut endpoints. If it is nonempty and $r\geq0$, then $$\operatorname{diam}\mathcal S_x(r)^2
 \leq8\left(r+\mathop{\mathrm{osc}}_{p\in\mathcal S_x(r)}v(\exp_xp)\right).$$

Let $(u,v)$ be a dual pair and $0<t<1$. Then $Q_tu=-Q_{1-t}v\in C^{1,1}(M)$, with almost-everywhere bounds $$-\frac{C_g}{1-t}g\leq\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}Q_tu\leq\frac{C_g}{t}g.$$ If $(x_t(z),p_t(z))=F_t^{-1}(z)$ and $\Phi_s$ is geodesic flow on $TM$, then $$(x_t(z),p_t(z))=\Phi_{-t}(z,\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}Q_tu(z)).$$ In particular, the pole and momentum maps are Lipschitz with constants depending only on $M,g,t$. There are also $r_t,b_t>0$, depending only on $M,g,t$, such that every $z=\exp_x(tp)$, $p\in\partial u(x)$, satisfies $$u(x')+c_t(x',z)\geq
 u(x)+c_t(x,z)+b_t d(x,x')^2
 \qquad\text{if }d(x,x')<r_t.$$ All these constants are uniform when $t$ ranges in a compact subinterval of $(0,1)$.

There is $c_{\rm p}>0$, depending only on $(M,g)$, with the following property. Let $y\in M$, $r\in T_yM$, and $1<T_*\le2$ satisfy $T_*r\in G_y$. Put $$\gamma(s)=\exp_y(sr),\quad x=\gamma(1),\quad
  p=-P_{y\to x}r,\quad L=(d\exp_x)_p,
  \qquad \tau=1+\frac{T_*-1}{2}.$$ Then all costs appearing in $$\label{spec:half-extension-gain}
  L^*\left[A_y(r)-\frac1\tau A_y(\tau r)\right]L
       \succeq c_{\rm p}(T_*-1)\mathrm{Id}$$ are smooth. If the terminal ray at time $T_*$ is nonconjugate, the same inequality holds with $\tau$ replaced by $T_*$ and its chosen smooth branch. In particular, for $T_*=1/l$ this latter inequality reads $$\label{spec:full-extension-gain}
  L^*\left[A_y(r)-l A_y(r/l)\right]L
       \succeq c_{\rm p}(1-l)\mathrm{Id},
       \qquad 1/2\le l<1.$$ Without any uniformity assertion, the source Hessian of divided action decreases strictly in the positive definite order between any two nonconjugate times on a minimizing ray.

If there are $\beta>0$, $C_0<\infty$, and $r_0>0$ such that $F(r)\leq C_0r^\beta$ for $0<r<r_0$, then all the optimal maps in the fixed density class have homeomorphic representatives with a common Hölder estimate in both directions. One may take any exponent no larger than $\frac12\min\{\beta,1\}$.

Suppose that $F$ has no power upper bound near zero. There are $r_j<R_j\to0$, pairs $(u_j,v_j)\in\mathcal C$, poles $x_j$, and numbers $a_j,D_j$ with $D_j>0$ such that $$\begin{gathered}
 \min_{S_{r_j}(x_j;u_j,v_j)}v_j=a_j,\qquad
 \max_{S_{r_j}(x_j;u_j,v_j)}v_j=a_j+D_j,               \label{sc:endlevels}\\
 \frac{r_j}{R_j}\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 F(R_j)\leq(1+\delta_j)D_j,\qquad \delta_j\longrightarrow0,\qquad
 \frac{|\log D_j|}{|\log R_j|}\longrightarrow0.       \label{sc:plateau-data}
\end{gathered}$$ Consequently $R_j/D_j^k\to0$ for every fixed $k>0$.

There is a fixed smooth function $B_c:\mathbb R\to(-1,1)$ with bounded derivatives such that $$B_c'<0\text{ on }\mathbb R,\qquad
 B_c(s)\geq1-\varepsilon_0\quad(s\leq1/2),\qquad
 B_c(s)<0\quad(s\geq3/4).$$ Given a cap $M_0\geq2$ and $K\geq1$, there are $0<\eta\leq1/128$ and a smooth bounded function $B_o\geq0$, with bounded derivatives, satisfying $$\begin{aligned}
 &B_o(s)\geq1\quad(s\leq1-\eta),\qquad
 B_o(1)=0,\qquad 1\leq B_o(0)\leq1+\varepsilon_0,       \label{sc:outer-values}\\
 &B_o(s)\geq B_o(0)+1
       \quad(1/16\leq s\leq1-\eta),            \label{sc:barrier}\\
 &B_o'(s)>0,\quad B_o''(s)\leq-K
       \quad\text{if }-2\eta\leq s\leq1-\eta
                      \text{ and }B_o(s)\leq M_0.     \label{sc:curvature}
\end{aligned}$$ One can arrange $\|B_o\|_\infty\leq2M_0+8$, independently of $K$, and make $\eta$ arbitrarily smaller if desired.

For all sufficiently small selected scales, uniformly for $b\in[b_-,b_+]$, there is $$\frac b{32D}\leq\tau_b\leq\frac{8b}D \label{sc:switch-time}$$ such that, at $x_b=\exp_{x_0}(\tau_b p_0)$, the function $g_b$ has active endpoints $y_-$ and $y_+$ with $$-2\eta\leq s_{y_-}<1/16,\qquad s_{y_+}\geq1-\eta.$$ The original endpoints $y_0,y_1$ and every active endpoint at this pole lie in one original section $S_{C b}(x_b;u,v)$, where $C$ depends only on the geometry and $H_o$. In particular every active level is in $[-\delta_j,1+\delta_j]$. For every minimizing log $q_i$ to an active endpoint, $$|q_i|^2=P-2D s_{y_i}+O_{H_o}(\tau_b+b) =P-2D s_{y_i}+o(D). \label{sc:switch-norms}$$ The constants in [sc:switch-time] are independent of $K$ and of the height and derivatives of the outer template.
For all sufficiently small selected scales and all $b\in[b_-,b_+]$, $$c_0b\leq E(b)\leq b, \label{sc:excess-bounds}$$ with the constant in [sc:numerical], independently of $K$.

Fix a sufficiently small selected scale. For every $t<1$ sufficiently close to one, the continuous function $$\Phi_t(b,z)=Q_tg_b(z)+Q_{1-t}w_{c,b}(z)-\pi(b),\qquad
 (b,z)\in[b_-,b_+]\times M,$$ has a positive global maximum with $b$ in the interior of its interval. Both spatial terms are $C^{1,1}$, and both minimizing points are unique. If $x$ and $y$ are these minimizing points at a maximum, there is $p\in\partial g_b(x)\cap G_x$ such that $$z=\exp_x(tp),\qquad y=\exp_xp,\qquad
 Q_tg_b(z)+Q_{1-t}w_{c,b}(z)=E_b(y)>0.
 \label{sc:aligned}$$ Moreover $(x,y)$ is before cut.

At any maximum in Lemma 22, let $$p=\sum_{i=1}^N m_i p_i,\qquad m_i>0,\qquad\sum_i m_i=1,$$ be any finite representation by minimizing logs active for the displayed representation $g_b=w_{o,b}^c$ at its minimizing pole $x$. Thus $g_b(x)+c(x,\exp_xp_i)+w_{o,b}(\exp_xp_i)=0$. Write $y_i=\exp_xp_i$ and $s_i=(v(y_i)-a)/D$, and let $s=(v(y)-a)/D$ be the center level. Then $$B_c(s)-\sum_i m_iB_o(s_i)\geq \pi'(b)\geq c_1. \label{sc:parameter-inequality}$$

At a maximum in Lemma 22, the center and all active endpoints belong to $S_{(H_o+2)b}(x;u,v)$. For every active log $p_i$, $$v(y_i)-v(y)=\frac{|p|^2-|p_i|^2}{2} +b\{B_c(s)-B_o(s_i)\}-E_b(y). \label{sc:level-identity}$$ In every positive barycentric representation the total weight on levels $s_i\geq1-\eta$ is at least $c_1$. Moreover $$s<3/4,\qquad \max\{s,s_i\}-\min\{s,s_i\}\leq1+\delta_j,\qquad \min\{s,s_i\}\geq-2\eta \label{sc:level-bounds}$$ for small scales. These conclusions hold at each exact maximum, before taking a prefix-time limit.

Suppose $p=\sum_{i=1}^N m_ip_i$ in an $n$-dimensional Euclidean space, with $N\leq n+1$, $m_i>0$, and $\sum_i m_i=1$. Suppose $E=\mathop{\mathrm{span}}\{p_i-p\}=\mathbb Re$, where $|e|=1$, and $q=p\cdot e>0$. Assume the template and level inequalities [sc:parameter-inequality], [sc:level-bounds], and $$\left|\ |p_i|^2-|p|^2+2D(s_i-s)\ \right|\leq\zeta D,\qquad 0\leq\delta_j\leq\zeta\leq1/16.$$ There is an outward index $i$ with $p_i=p+d_i e$, $d_i>0$, such that $$\begin{gathered} m_i\geq m_*:=\frac{c_1}{12(n+1)},\qquad m_id_i\geq\frac{c_1D}{8(n+1)q},\qquad d_i\leq\frac{3D}{2q}, \label{sc:outward-weight}\\ 0<|p_i|^2-|p|^2\leq3D, \label{sc:outward-norm}\\ -2\eta\leq s_i<1-\eta,\qquad B_o(s_i)\leq1/m_*. \label{sc:outward-cap} \end{gathered}$$ In particular the cap $M_0=2/m_*$ can be fixed before $K$. All these constants are independent of $K$.

Let $u,v$ be the dual potentials for an admissible pair of densities, and let $$\mathcal C=\{(x,y):u(x)+c(x,y)+v(y)=0\}.$$ For a Borel set $A$ on either side, its contact image satisfies $$\label{jet:contact-volume-eq}
 \frac{\lambda}{\Lambda}\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(A)
 \le \mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(\mathcal C(A))
 \le \frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}\mathop{\mathrm{vol}}(A).$$ Projections are interpreted in the completed volume measures.

Let $v$ be one of the original dual potentials. Suppose a $C^2$ function $\phi$ touches $v$ from below at $y$, its gradient $r=\mathop{\mathrm{grad}}\phi(y)$ belongs to $I(y)$, and $$W=\mathop{\mathrm{Hess}}\phi(y)+A_y(r)>0.$$ Then $$\label{jet:viscosity-eq}
 \sigma_y(r)\det W\le \Lambda/\lambda.$$ The same conclusion holds for a lower Taylor jet with these properties, by approximation of its quadratic part.

Fix $b>0$ and an active outer pair $$g_b(x)+c(x,y)+\varphi_o(v(y))=0.$$ Choose any minimizing reverse log $r$ from $y$ to $x$. Suppose $$l=\varphi_o'(v(y))>1,\qquad \varphi_o''(v(y))<0.$$ Then the chosen modified ray is nonconjugate at its endpoint. The true log $r/l$ is before cut.

If $f$ is semiconvex near $0$ and has the Alexandrov expansion $$f(h)=f(0)+p\cdot h+\tfrac12 A(h,h)+o(|h|^2),$$ then every nearby subgradient satisfies $$\zeta=p+Ah+o(|h|),\qquad \zeta\in\partial f(h),$$ uniformly over the choice of $\zeta$.

Fix the center template and the constants of Lemmas 21, 22, 23, and 25. Choose $K$, then an outer template with curvature less than $-K$ in the prescribed capped region. For all sufficiently small scales in the sequence of Lemma 18, there are a parameter $b\in[b_-,b_+]$, a pole $x$, center and active logs $p,p_i\in G_x$, weights $m_i>0$ summing to one, and symmetric matrices $H,L,V,V_i$ on $T_xM$, with the following properties. For one selected index $i$, $$\begin{gathered} p=\sum_jm_jp_j,\qquad E=\mathop{\mathrm{span}}\{p_j-p\}=\mathbb Re,\qquad |e|=1,\quad q=p\cdot e>0,\quad q^2\ge cD, \label{jet:limiting-geometry}\\ m_i\ge m_*>0,\qquad p_i=p+d_ie,\quad d_i>0, \label{jet:limiting-outward}\\ L\ge0,\qquad LE=0,\qquad H\le L,\qquad H\ge V+c\frac bD\mathrm{Id}-C\frac b{D^2}pp^*,\qquad V>0, \label{jet:limiting-center}\\ V_i\ge m_iL+cK\frac b{D^2}p_ip_i^*,\qquad V_i>0. \label{jet:limiting-outer} \end{gathered}$$ The center modified log and the selected outer modified log are nonconjugate. Let $r$ and $r_i$ denote the reverse logs of these specified rays, let $y=\exp_xp$, $y_i=\exp_xp_i$, and set $l=\varphi_c'(v(y))$, $l_i=\varphi_o'(v(y_i))$. The chosen true limiting branches are also nonconjugate, and $$\label{jet:limiting-determinants} \det V\ge c\,\frac{\sigma_x(p)^2}{\sigma_y(r/l)}, \qquad \det V_i\le C\,\frac{\sigma_x(p_i)^2}{\sigma_{y_i}(r_i/l_i)}.$$ Here $c,C,m_*$ are independent of $K$ and the outer template. The level and norm-increment conclusions of Lemma 25 hold as well.

Suppose the matrices and vectors satisfy [jet:limiting-geometry]–[jet:limiting-outer]. Then $$\label{jet:matrix-gain} \det V_i\ge cK\det V,$$ where $c>0$ depends on the fixed center-template constants, the dimension, and $m_*$, and is independent of $K$.
The section-oscillation function of Lemma 18 has a positive power upper bound at zero.
